parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

Study Fig. 4.1, which is a map of earthquakes in part of South America in the 21^st^ century.

![Map showing earthquake focal depths in Chile and Argentina, along the Nazca and South American Plate boundary, with directional arrows and a colour-coded key.](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2025/09/43312_screenshot-2025-09-22-091941.png)

Explain why the depth of focus changes from **A** to **B** in Fig. 4.1.
parts.solution_md:
The depth increases towards B because the plates are converging **[1]** and the Nazca Plate is subducting **[1] **which means that the plate is getting deeper as it moves east. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word '**explain**' means that the answer should include supporting details and explanations for how or why something occurs or is the way it is.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - One mark [1] for each valid point (up to a maximum of 3 marks)
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - The oceanic plate is subducted
> - The plate is denser/heavier
> - The subduction zone gets deeper towards the east

> **[exam-tip]**
> For this question it is important to understand that the plate boundary is not a single line but a zone. The line shows the point on the surface where the subduction zone starts, the depth of the subduction zone increases with distance from that line.

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig 1.1, which shows an earthquake at a plate boundary.

![Seismic illustration showing concentric circles from point X, depicting plate movement from Plate A to Plate B, with trees, car, and cityscape above.](assets/003-seismic-illustration-showing-concentric-circles-.png)

*Fig 1.1*

Explain why earthquakes occur at plate boundaries, such as the one shown in Fig 1.1.
parts.solution_md:
The plates are moving towards each other **[1] **the subduction plate goes underneath the other plate **[1] **because it is more dense.** [1] **Pressure builds up when the plates stick** [1] **eventually the jolt free causing an earthquake. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **'explain**,' which means that the answer needs to provide reasons for how and why the earthquake happened.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark** [1]** for each valid point (up to a maximum of 5 marks).
> 
> OR
> 
> - 3 marks for 3 valid points and 2 marks for developing two of those points.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Convergent boundary
> - Friction
> - Energy release

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig 1.1, which shows an earthquake at a plate boundary.

![Diagram of tectonic plates showing an earthquake focus at point X, seismic wave circles, plates A and B, trees, a car, buildings, and plate movement direction.](assets/004-diagram-of-tectonic-plates-showing-an-earthquake.png)

*Fig 1.1*

Identify the features labelled X, Y and Z on Fig 1.1.

Explain why a volcanic eruption occurred in a detailed specific example you have studied.

Name of detailed specific example.....................................................................
parts.solution_md:
The 2021 Cumbre Vieja eruption occurred on La Palma in the Canary Islands, which is located above a volcanic hotspot **[KU]**. The Canary Islands are formed by a mantle plume **[KU]**, where hot magma rises from deep within the Earth's mantle towards the surface **[KU]**. As the African Plate moves slowly over this stationary hotspot, volcanic activity creates a chain of islands **[KU]**.  On 19th September 2021, the pressure from the rising magma finally overcame the strength of the overlying rock **[KU]**. The eruption began with explosive activity followed by effusive lava flows that continued for 85 days, destroying over 1,600 buildings **[KU]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> The command word is **'explain'**, which means that the answer needs to outline the causes of volcanic eruptions and the processes which occur.
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1 knowledge and understanding **[KU]**
> 
> - A top-level 3 [7 mark] answer will include specific examples that show:
> 
> - Knowledge of processes
> - Understanding of how these processes led to a named eruption
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Volcanic eruptions occur at divergent and convergent plate boundaries
> - Hotspot volcanoes can occur away from plate boundaries
> - Different types of magma produce different eruption styles
> - Most active volcanoes occur around the Pacific Ring of Fire

> **[exam-tip]**
> When asked for detailed specific example it is important to relate the processes to that example. In the answer above it is not as simple as stating that magma rises from the mantle - showing your place specific knowledge means being able to name the location, the type of volcanic setting, and specific details about the eruption sequence.

parts.problem_md:
Explain why an earthquake occurred in a detailed specific example you have studied.

Name of detailed specific example.....................................................................
parts.solution_md:
The 2023 Türkiye–Syria earthquake occurred along the East Anatolian Fault, which is a transform plate boundary **[KU]**. At this boundary, the Arabian Plate is slowly moving northwards while the Anatolian Plate is being pushed westwards **[KU]**. Because the plates do not slide smoothly, friction causes them to become stuck **[KU]**, even though the plates continue to move** [KU]**. This results in enormous stress building up in the crust over hundreds of years **[KU]**. Eventually, in February 2023, the pressure was suddenly released in a violent jolt, producing a magnitude 7.8 earthquake **[KU].** The focus was shallow, which meant seismic waves reached the surface quickly and caused intense shaking that damaged buildings across a wide area **[KU]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> The command word is **'explain**,' which means that the answer needs to outline the causes of earthquakes and the processes which occur.
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1 knowledge and understanding **[KU]**
> 
> - A top-level 3 [7 mark] answer will include specific examples that show:
> 
>   - Knowledge of processes
>   - Understanding of how these processes led to a named earthquake
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Earthquakes occur at all plate boundaries
> - Shallow earthquakes are more likely at divergent boundaries
> - Stronger earthquakes tend to occur at convergent, collision and transform boundaries
> - Most earthquakes occur around the Pacific Ring of Fire - approximately 90%

> **[exam-tip]**
> When asked for detailed specific example it is important to relate the processes to that example. In the answer above it is not as simple as stating that the plates move past one another showing your place specific knowledge means being able to name the plates and which direction they are moving.

parts.problem_md:
The strongest earthquake in history was at Bio-Bio in Chile, in 1960, with a magnitude of 9.5. The location of Bio-Bio is shown in Fig. 3.1.

![q3a-0460_w20_qp_21](assets/005-q3a-0460-w20-qp-21.png)

Using evidence from Fig. 3.1, explain the cause of the Bio-Bio earthquake.
parts.solution_md:
Bio-Bio is close to a plate boundary. **[1] **The South American and Nazca plate are moving towards each other. **[1] **As they collide they may get stuck causing pressure to build up. **[1] **Eventually they jolt free releasing the energy as seismic waves.** [1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **'explain**,' which means that the answer needs to provide reasons for how and why the earthquake happened.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark** [1]** for each valid point (up to a maximum of 4 marks)
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Subduction (or description of subduction), of oceanic plate
> - Oceanic denser/continental less dense
> - Friction, compression/pressure
> - Fracturing/faulting
> - Release of energy

parts.problem_md: Explain how an earthquake occurs at a conservative plate margin
parts.solution_md:
At a conservative plate margin, two plates slide past each other in different directions **[1]** As plates move friction occurs **[1]** The plates get stuck but still try to move and so pressure builds up **[1]** When the pressure is released, the energy released is an earthquake. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word ‘**explain**’ requires you to outline the process of  how earthquakes occur.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1] **for each valid part of the process
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - The plates move in the same direction but at different speeds.
> - Plates jolt free.
> - Energy passes through the Earth's crust in waves.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Take care to read the question carefully. It is easy to confuse the different types of plate boundary. Although the earthquake process is similar at all plate boundaries you will be expected to write about the direction of plate movement.

parts.problem_md:
Figure 1.3 shows information about a volcanic eruption on Whakaari.

![Cross-section diagram of a volcanic eruption showing ash, gases, lava, and volcanic bombs with labelled tectonic plates and subduction zone beneath.](assets/009-cross-section-diagram-of-a-volcanic-eruption-sho.png)

Use Figure 1.3 to explain why a volcanic eruption occurred on Whakaari.
parts.solution_md:
The Pacific Plate and the Indo-Australian Plate are moving towards each other **[1]**. The Pacific Plate is more dense **[1] **and so goes underneath the Indo-Australian Plate (subduction) **[1]**. This leads to the friction and heat so the crust melts** [1]** . The magma then rises to the surface, leading to a volcanic eruption** [1]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is 'explain' means to give a reason to show why volcanic eruptions occur. Avoid just describing — focus on why or how, not just what.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - One mark will be awarded for each point made.
> - To gain five marks the answer needs to outline five steps in the process.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of a response to this question. Other information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Build up of magma
> - Pressure/energy build up
> - Plates are converging
